name: Christian Anarchism
summary: Christian anarchism holds that Jesus' teaching, above all the Sermon on the Mount's call to non-resistance and love of enemies, is incompatible with the state, which rests on violence and claims an allegiance owed only to God. Adherents are overwhelmingly pacifist, reject war, oaths and military service, favour voluntary poverty, sharing and servant leadership, and distrust hierarchical churches. Methods are nonviolent: refusal, civil disobedience and community, not revolution or politics.
scope: The mainstream pacifist strand: Tolstoy (The Kingdom of God Is Within You, drawing on Ballou, Garrison and Chelcicky), Jacques Ellul (Anarchism and Christianity) and the Catholic Worker tradition of Dorothy Day and Ammon Hennacy. Excludes violent Christian revolutionary movements and non-anarchist Christian socialism. Many answers on modern issues are low-confidence inferences because the sources focus on the state, violence and property.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Christian anarchists hold that care for the sick is a duty of believers and voluntary communities (as in the Catholic Worker's hospitality), not of a coercive state; support for the aim but not the state mechanism is inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: A state-set wage is a law enforced by force, which they reject; they favour voluntary justice toward workers and simple living. Inferred from the anti-state principle.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Ellul calls money the domain of Mammon, and the movement favours sharing goods over competition, so markets are not credited with superior allocation; they distrust government equally.

public-ownership.rationale: State ownership would enlarge the violent state they consider illegitimate; they prefer voluntary sharing and community.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Ballou's catechism, reproduced by Tolstoy, says Christians should not voluntarily pay taxes yet not resist them, so they would not call on the state to tax anyone; they urge the rich to give voluntarily.

unions-good.rationale: Adherents split: Catholic Worker figures backed labour solidarity, while others reject organised coercive pressure; the sources do not settle it.

property-fundamental.rationale: Helchitsky as reported by Tolstoy says a Christian cannot even be a landowner, and the early church shared goods; property is not a right to be protected by force.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Regulation means state coercion, which they oppose, though they condemn corporate power; inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: They would not defend state welfare as such, but cutting aid to the poor contradicts Jesus' teaching on charity; they want it replaced by voluntary giving, not simply abolished.

worker-ownership.rationale: Sharing of labour and goods in early Christian communities and Catholic Worker communes is admired; the voluntary form fits, though it is not a defined programme.

surveillance-ok.rationale: They reject state violence and its security justifications, and refuse ends-justify-means reasoning.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No source addresses it; adherents divide between libertarian and ascetic views.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: They oppose enforcing speech laws with state force while condemning hatred morally; inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: Ellul holds the state illegitimate and concentrated authority hostile to Christian freedom; Jesus' model is servant leadership.

state-harmful.rationale: Ellul says the state is illegitimate and must be destroyed unless it serves all; Wikipedia describes the state as violent, deceitful and idolatrous in their view.

limit-guns.rationale: They are pacifists who reject owning arms for violence, but oppose state coercion to disarm; adherents are split.

empower-police-military.rationale: Tolstoy calls on Christians to refuse military service, and they reject state violence entirely.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: No documented position; the movement mixes personal moral conservatism with opposition to state penalties.

decide-locally.rationale: They prefer horizontal, small-scale, voluntary human relations over hierarchy, which favours local decision.

rehabilitation.rationale: Love of enemies and forgiveness reject retribution; Tolstoy argues government force cannot suppress evil.

traditional-family.rationale: Adherents divide; the movement's sources focus on nonviolence and the state, not family structure.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Christian anarchists are divided on the underlying ethics while generally opposing state control of marriage.

abortion-legal.rationale: Many Catholic Worker-linked adherents oppose abortion, others do not; they split and the state's role is rejected anyway.

more-religion-public.rationale: They oppose state-church alliance since Constantine; Christianity should be lived, not backed by public power, though they are devout.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Christ's call to serve the oppressed supports addressing injustice, but by voluntary and nonviolent action; inferred.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; inferred from their general principles of nonviolence and rejection of state authority.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Tolstoy lists renouncing national distinctions among Christian commands; they hold that all mankind are countrymen.

gradual-change.rationale: They reject deference to state institutions, though Ellul prefers persistent small refusals over sudden revolution; so not respecting institutions outweighs.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Garrison's declaration endorsed by Tolstoy: our country is the world; state border enforcement is state violence.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Any larger government is still a human government to which Christians give no allegiance.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed; they criticise both capitalism and state power; inferred from their general principles of nonviolence and rejection of state authority.

nation-first.rationale: Tolstoy renounces national distinctions and patriotism as contrary to Christ's teaching.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Military action is rejected even to resist evil; non-resistance is central.

open-borders.rationale: Our country is the world; they reject the state's authority to bar people.

limit-growth.rationale: Voluntary poverty and simple living are widely advocated; inferred.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: No documented position; the state-led form would be rejected, while stewardship is accepted.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Ellul was a leading critic of technique and its domination of human life.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Inferred from anti-militarism and simple living; not addressed.

revolution-justified.rationale: Violent revolution is rejected; Garrison called the spirit of Jacobinism one of retaliation and murder.

experts-over-public.rationale: Hierarchy of any kind is opposed; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Central planning is state power; Ellul says the state is illegitimate unless it serves all.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed directly; voluntary cooperatives fit, state ownership does not; inferred from their general principles of nonviolence and rejection of state authority.

land-value-tax.rationale: A tax is state coercion; Helchitsky doubted landownership but the tax solution is not their programme.

tax-inheritance.rationale: They do not advocate state taxation, though Ballou's catechism accepts non-resisting taxes.

basic-income.rationale: A state programme funded by coercion, though sharing with the poor is a Christian duty; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Nationalist economic policy contradicts renouncing national distinctions.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Increases state power, which they consider illegitimate.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Dorothy Day's distributism is compared to Proudhon's mutualism, but others favour communal sharing; split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Ellul calls money the domain of Mammon, but abolition is not a programme for most adherents.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Not addressed; they oppose both state and market power; inferred from their general principles of nonviolence and rejection of state authority.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies are state machinery; they reject.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Christian anarchists cite the Old Testament demand for a king as a fall into coercive authority and see all rulers as non-binding.

democracy-best.rationale: Ballou's catechism says taking part in elections is participation in government by force; they do not see democracy as a legitimate authority either.

direct-votes.rationale: They reject voting as participation in force, yet horizontal decisions in communities are valued; split.

workers-councils.rationale: They want horizontal organisation but not political power as such; not addressed.

right-to-secede.rationale: Denial of the state's authority implies this right; inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: They hold God alone as authority and favour servant leadership and horizontal relations.

political-violence-never.rationale: Most are pacifists who reject violence even in response to violence and hold that ends never justify means.

war-builds-character.rationale: War is condemned as incompatible with Christ's teaching.

separate-church-state.rationale: They condemn the Constantinian union of church and state as corruption, so separation is favoured, though they see the state as illegitimate anyway.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: They reject coercive law of any kind; Christian teaching is for personal obedience, not state enforcement.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Garrison's declaration says Christians cannot sue at law and all violent defence is rejected.

military-superiority.rationale: Tolstoy condemns the arms race that is exhausting the European states and says each man called up should refuse to serve in the army at all.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Renouncing national distinctions; all mankind are countrymen.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Ellul broke with Marx and rejects violent struggle; Christian love is the alternative.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not addressed by sources; inferred from their general principles of nonviolence and rejection of state authority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; reparations require state power though repentance is valued; inferred from their general principles of nonviolence and rejection of state authority.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; coercion would be rejected; inferred from their general principles of nonviolence and rejection of state authority.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Voluntary simple living is admired but not foraging.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Reject the state's authority and legal-political methods; a constitutional document enforced by government is not their route. Inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from Tolstoy's condemnation of conquest and violence as bases of state claims.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred from Ellul's view that all rulers' authority is illegitimate before God, however chosen.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from the primacy of individual conscience before God over any collective command.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Non-resistance to evil is central to Tolstoy's reading of the Sermon on the Mount, so removing a ruler by force is rejected; disobedience remains allowed.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Inferred from rejection of state legislative authority generally.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Inferred from Tolstoy's ethics of compassion and vegetarianism.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from the ethic of love and non-violence extended to animals.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Voluntary poverty, sharing and servant leadership are central, and the Sermon on the Mount commands care for the poor.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Inferred from non-participation in politics and refusal of state allegiance; adherents still serve their communities.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred from Ellul's critique of propaganda and mass society.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred from Ellul's account of how states win allegiance through ideology and institutions.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred from Tolstoy's critique of exploitation of the poor by the rich and the state.

native-born-offices.rationale: Tolstoy's critique of patriotism and nation is central to his argument against state allegiance.

party-own-road.rationale: Christian anarchists do not address communist party relations.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from voluntary community; the question of foreign aid is not addressed.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Rejection of war and patriotic claims is central to the Christian anarchist position.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Inferred from rejection of rule by any group over another.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: They oppose fascism but place no faith in state constitutions.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Inferred from equal condemnation of the violence of all states.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred from Tolstoy and the abolitionists Ballou and Garrison, on whom the tradition draws.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from rejection of state glorification of violence and heroes.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from the universal commandment to love one's neighbour.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from non-violence and love of neighbour applying equally to all.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: They reject all government, so the premise is not addressed.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Tolstoy rejects military service and war, so a political role for armed forces is rejected.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from a gift ethic of voluntary service rather than wage labour.

filial-duty.rationale: Honouring parents is a biblical commandment and family care is part of the sharing ethic, though Jesus also subordinates family ties; inferred from the Christian sources.

office-by-exam.rationale: Tolstoy and Ellul reject taking part in state office at all, so how posts are filled is not their concern; examination-selected rulers are still rulers, so mild disagreement is inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Tolstoy condemns patriotism and national exclusion as contrary to Christian brotherhood; state protection of national firms is inferred to be rejected.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Jesus' teaching restricts divorce, yet Christian anarchists object to state regulation of marriage; adherents are inferred to split between personal teaching and legal freedom.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Servant leadership and rejection of hierarchy favour accountable, instructed representatives, though adherents mostly refuse office rather than seek such rules; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Voluntary sharing and mutual care are favoured over both state schemes and profit-seeking private firms; private market accounts are inferred to be disfavoured.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Tolstoy argued that land should not be private property and Christian anarchists favour sharing and voluntary poverty; use-based tenure is inferred from this.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Christian anarchists deny the state's legitimacy and refuse to take part in it, so they would not endorse parliamentary control of its spending; inferred.

single-official-language.rationale: Rejecting state coercion and nationalism, they would not back state enforcement of one language; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Tolstoy rejects patriotism and national barriers as unchristian, and opposes private land monopoly in any case; a citizens-only rule is inferred to be rejected.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The sources do not address outcome-based discrimination law; concern for the oppressed is offset by distrust of state remedies, so adherents are taken as split.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Voluntary poverty, sharing and the rejection of mammon are core Christian anarchist themes, and Ellul treats money as a power opposed to God.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Non-resistance and love of enemies are the core of the doctrine, and Tolstoy rejects all state violence and war.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Tolstoy and Ellul reject military force by states and the use of troops against others, whatever the justification.

corporate-influence.rationale: Ellul and the Catholic Worker tradition criticise money and wealth as powers; corporate lobbying is inferred as one case.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Adherents resist state claims to enforce national loyalty; no source addresses funding, so this is inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Adherents distrust state programmes and nationalist population goals, though they value family; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Voluntary sharing and hospitality are favoured over coercive exclusion by authorities; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: Voluntary poverty and mutual aid are preferred to state programmes; the state acting as employer is inferred to be unwelcome.

democratic-peace.rationale: Ellul and Tolstoy treat all states, democratic or not, as resting on violence, so spreading democracy is not a path to peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Tolstoy argues allegiance is owed to God, not the state, and refuses oaths and obedience to commands that conflict with Jesus.

non-intervention.rationale: Pacifism opposes military intervention, though adherents would not frame it as a state right; mostly inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is not a concern of the sources and adherents have no shared view.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Love of enemies and rejection of nationalism rule out blaming a minority for a conspiracy.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Adherents distrust state authority but also value marriage as a Christian practice; no source settles it.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Distrust of state secrecy suggests support, but the sources do not discuss it; inferred.

local-production.rationale: The Catholic Worker tradition favours small, communal and agrarian living; inferred as a mild yes.

informal-organisation.rationale: Adherents favour voluntary community and refusal over parties and political organising; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Tolstoy rejects patriotism and national sovereignty as a claim on conscience, so national precedence is not accepted.

religious-nation.rationale: Tolstoy and Ellul reject patriotism and tie the Kingdom of God to no nation, so a creed-defined nation is refused.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Tolstoy and Ellul reject state power and honor, so ritual submission to a leading power is opposed; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Voluntary sharing and poverty imply giving to those in need over hoarding by region; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Adherents favor sharing and voluntary poverty, and Tolstoy opposed land ownership, but the statement's framing of common means of production is not addressed.

defeat-communism.rationale: Pacifism and love of enemies imply coexistence and nonviolence, not a campaign to defeat communism; inferred.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Adherents reject coerced state systems and favor voluntary provision; inferred from the audit's health answer.

religion-illusion.rationale: Faith in Jesus' teaching is central, so religion as a mere illusion is rejected.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Ellul's critique of money and power makes capitalism a regressive force; inferred.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The sources do not address women's equality or economic change.

socialized-care.rationale: Care is a duty of believers and voluntary communities, not a public service; inferred.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Tolstoy's critique of patriotism and nationalism makes language purism unlikely; inferred.

treaties-binding.rationale: Adherents distrust state authority but value keeping one's word; they do not address such treaties.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Voluntary sharing and communities like the Catholic Worker houses are central, though not all hold property in common.

majority-settlement.rationale: Non-resistance and rejection of nationalism oppose state-promoted settlement of the majority; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Rejecting both the state and capitalism, adherents look to voluntary Christian community; inferred.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Christian anarchists reject national and state claims to territory and hold that allegiance is owed to God alone; a rejection of land claims grounded in history or religion is inferred from this.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Nothing in the tradition supports denial, and its commitment to truth-telling and love of neighbour makes denial of a mass atrocity against a people unthinkable; inferred from those principles.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Christian anarchists reject state coercion and punishment in matters of conscience and morals, so they would oppose criminal penalties whatever their personal views on sexual ethics.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Tolstoy and Ellul reject the state's violence and coercion as such, including its use to silence dissent, and call for nonviolent resistance to it.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Tolstoy argues that church and state have used violence to enforce belief against Jesus' teaching of non-resistance, so punishment of blasphemy by civil government is rejected.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Tolstoy condemns governments' wars and exploitation for the benefit of ruling classes, and the tradition rejects state power in general, so colonial rule for economic gain is rejected.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: The tradition holds that Christians must not take up arms even in defence and must love enemies; by extension it rejects any religious duty to armed resistance, an extension inferred from its non-resistance.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Christian anarchists reject armed overthrow of rulers as strongly as rule itself, holding that violence cannot establish a godly order; Tolstoy insists on non-resistance even to evil governments.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Ellul and Catholic Worker communities favour small, face-to-face, voluntary decision-making over distant officials, though adherents also abstain from state politics; this is inferred from their communitarian practice.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Adherents oppose domination of every kind but the tradition does not use the intersectional framework, and its focus on the state, violence and property leaves the claim neither endorsed nor rejected.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: The tradition says little on this, and modern Christian anarchists differ between compassion for trans people and traditional views, while rejecting state coercion either way; adherents are split.

assisted-dying.rationale: Reverence for life and the Catholic Worker tradition's opposition to killing suggest that most adherents would reject helping end life, though the tradition's dislike of state control of medicine tempers this; inferred.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Christian anarchists place themselves outside state politics and both left and right as Ellul and Tolstoy describe them, but the claim that the best ideas of each should be combined is an inference.

alienated-labor.rationale: Tolstoy and the Catholic Worker criticize wage labor and industrial work that serves the rich, and favour manual, communal work, but the Marxist concept of alienation is not their own; inferred.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Christian anarchists teach love of enemies and non-resistance and reject nationalism and the clash of cultures, so they would not call another faith incompatible with their society; inferred from these principles.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Christian anarchists hold that only God holds legitimate authority and reject the state's claim to it, but they deny that this makes any human government legitimate, so agreement with the statement is qualified.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Adherents reject state compulsion in religion and favour freedom of conscience, which suggests opposing a ban on religious dress; the tradition never addresses it, so this is inferred.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: The tradition's concern for the weak against the powerful suggests support for ending secrecy that shields abusers, though it distrusts state legislation as a remedy; inferred.

social-market-economy.rationale: Christian anarchists reject both capitalism and the state regulating it, favouring voluntary sharing and community, so a state-managed mix of market and welfare is not their ideal; inferred.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Tolstoy says Christians must refuse military service and Ellul and the Catholic Worker reject war, so abolishing armies is central to the tradition.

rich-first.rationale: Christian anarchists favour voluntary poverty, sharing of goods and care for the poor, and reject letting some grow rich first; inferred from Sermon on the Mount teaching on wealth.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Tolstoy and the Catholic Worker oppose participation in all wars and military alliances, which implies keeping out of rival blocs.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Christian anarchists reject all earthly rulers and hereditary kingship as a claim to an allegiance owed only to God (Tolstoy, Ellul read 1 Samuel 8 as a rebuke of monarchy).

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Their ban on usury and stress on voluntary sharing and mutual aid (Catholic Worker tradition) suggest sympathy for interest-free, user-owned credit; inferred, not a stated programme.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: The sources do not address international lenders; sympathy for the poor pulls toward refusal, but anti-state, anti-nationalist principle gives no reason to defend a government's economic sovereignty.

property-franchise.rationale: They abstain from voting altogether and hold wealth a spiritual danger, so tying political rights to property runs against their principles; inferred, since they reject the state's franchise itself.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Opposition to domination in all forms and Ellul's critique of technological power make sympathy plausible, but the sources do not discuss the ecofeminist claim; inferred.

reification.rationale: Ellul and the tradition condemn Mammon and money as a power that rules people, which resembles the claim; the Marxist framing is not theirs, so this is inferred.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Their view that wealth corrupts and that the powerful dominate the poor suggests agreement that wealth shapes who is heard; the sources do not address the press, so it is inferred.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: They hold that all state law rests on coercion and that Christians should obey God's law rather than rulers; they would not endorse rule through state courts, though arbitrary decree is no better. Inferred.

racial-franchise.rationale: Their universal love and Tolstoy's rejection of patriotism and national distinctions oppose limiting political rights by race, and they reject the state's franchise anyway.

online-participation.rationale: They refuse to take part in government by voting or office, and Ellul distrusts technique, so online political participation is unlikely to appeal; inferred.

open-government-data.rationale: They reject the state, so the question of how it should handle records is not one they address; secrecy is disliked but they do not seek to improve government.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Their rejection of coercive state law and their universal-love ethic oppose legal limits on whom adults may marry.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The command to love one's enemies and Tolstoy's rejection of national and religious enmity oppose shunning people by their faith.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Christian anarchists distrust state institutions but favour consensus-based voluntary communities; whether sortition bodies would count is inferred from that, so they are split.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Tolstoy and Ellul read scripture against church tradition and authority, so rethinking inherited doctrine is inferred to be welcome, though they appeal to the Gospels rather than to modernity.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Ellul and the Catholic Worker treat the pursuit of wealth as service to Mammon and favour sharing and voluntary poverty, so accumulations of money are seen as corrupting power.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Adherents reject military service for everyone, but nothing in the sources bears on who may serve; they would not defend a ban on gay people serving. Inferred from non-resistance.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Faith is a matter of conscience, and a state forcing belief or unbelief is exactly the coercion they reject; Tolstoy and Ellul oppose state control of religion.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Tolstoy rejects violent punishment and coercive government, and they favour nonviolent community means of dealing with wrongdoing; most adherents would still not call for abolition by political action.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: They reject state power altogether rather than seeking a better balance within it; inferred from the anti-state principle, with no source on power-sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Voluntary hospitality and mutual aid among believers, as in the Catholic Worker, is their model for helping the poor in place of the state.

term-limits.rationale: They abstain from office rather than reform its terms; inferred from the refusal to take part in government.

vote-delegation.rationale: Ballou's catechism cited by Tolstoy counts voting as sharing in state force, so a system for exercising votes is unattractive; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The sources never address extinction risk; adherents focus on non-violence and trust in God rather than state risk programmes.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Their distrust of church hierarchy and emphasis on servant leadership point toward open offices, though the sources do not address this directly.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Rejection of domination and the Sermon's teaching of mutual service point to shared authority; inferred, not stated in the sources.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Allegiance is owed to God rather than to a nation, so excluding resident foreigners from local politics has no basis; inferred.

rent-control.rationale: A legal rent cap is enforced by state force, which they reject, though they favour just treatment of tenants; inferred.

abolish-ip.rationale: Tolstoy and Ellul distrust property claims and favour sharing, so state-enforced monopolies on ideas are inferred to be unwelcome.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Tolstoy treats military training and drilling for the state as incompatible with Christ's teaching.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Their rejection of war and violence rules out nuclear weapons anywhere; the position is implied rather than stated about territory.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Rejecting war and military service, they oppose military bases, foreign or domestic; implied by core pacifism.

recognise-genocide.rationale: They condemn genocide but distrust state acts; formal government recognition is not addressed, so inferred as split.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Voluntary poverty and sharing, and Ellul's critique of property, favour rewarding work over mere ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Tolstoy's Kingdom of God Is Within You rules out killing even to resist evil, including in defence of others.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: They treat nations as state constructs and reject nationalism; inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents split.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents split.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Tolstoy condemns patriotic cult of the nation; martyrdom is reserved for Christ and faith, not nation. Inferred.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Adherents read Christian life as a struggle between God and worldly power, but they reject force in it; inferred.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed; indifference follows from rejecting national states.

culture-before-state.rationale: They favour change through example and community rather than state action; inferred.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents split.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; they judge texts by the Sermon on the Mount rather than by women's humanity, adherents split.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Nationality has no weight for those who reject nations and serve all as neighbours; inferred.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Redrawing state units for one people is a state project they reject; inferred.

independent-unions.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic Worker's support for workers' voluntary organisation against both employers and the state.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; Christian anarchists criticise capitalism but do not define socialism, so adherents split.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the view that care for others is a duty of voluntary communities, not a coercive state, though local commons are not opposed.

second-chamber.rationale: Inferred from Ellul's view that political institutions have no legitimacy for Christians, so adding a state chamber is not wanted.

municipal-property.rationale: Christian anarchists favour sharing and voluntary community of goods, but the sources do not decide on municipal ownership.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Inferred from their preference for small voluntary communities that cooperate without coercive central authority.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from the Catholic Worker's concern that workers be paid justly enough to live, though sources do not state it.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; no principle of the tradition settles the speed-versus-safety trade-off.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from the rejection of state funding via taxation and a view that accepting mortality is part of human limits.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Ellul sees money and state power as entwined and Christian anarchists refuse tax payments; inferred support for payments beyond state control.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from distrust of state power and surveillance; not discussed in the sources.

person-over-state.rationale: Ellul and Tolstoy hold that obedience is owed to God and conscience, not the state, and that no person may be used as a means by it.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Christian anarchism is grounded in the spiritual life and teaching of Jesus, with material concerns subordinate.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from rejection of final state authority at any level; the sources do not discuss regional devolution.

gm-crops.rationale: Not addressed by the sources; adherents split between technological and simple-living outlooks.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed; Catholic Worker houses are urban while Tolstoyan communities were rural, so adherents split.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Tolstoy rejects patriotism and national divisions as contrary to Christian brotherhood, and the same reasoning rules out racial blocs.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from Tolstoy's condemnation of patriotic pride and from Christian humility and universal brotherhood.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Tolstoy's non-resistance rejects all military service and violence, including war in defence of the country.

missingStatements.text: A person should refuse to serve in the armed forces even when the law requires it.
missingStatements.rationale: Tolstoy says the Christian's duty is to refuse meekly but firmly to serve in the army.

missingStatements.text: Sworn oaths of allegiance to the state or its officials are wrong.
missingStatements.rationale: Tolstoy and Ballou read the Sermon's ban on oaths as forbidding binding oaths and allegiance oaths.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow to Christian and a few pacifist traditions (Quakers, Anabaptists); few other ideologies in the bank would take a side, so it would not separate ideologies.

missingStatements.text: Citizens should not take part in government by voting or holding office.
missingStatements.rationale: Ballou's catechism, reproduced by Tolstoy, calls participation in election and government participation in force; Hennacy and others abstained, though not all adherents agree.

notes: Ellul read Romans 13 as a reason not to overthrow the state, while Hennacy and O'Reilly favoured civil disobedience; strands differ on voting, taxes and the Church. Only part of the long Wikipedia and Tolstoy texts was read.
